doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Five years in the army
summary: He stayed in as a musician, rose to corporal, tried to get out, and was kept to play shows.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So when you started at Fort McLellan in the army, you got your basic training and then you have your AIT, Advanced Infantry Training. So were you re-stationed anywhere or did you serve your whole time right there at Fort McLellan?
I was stationed in Fort McLellan but I was all over the country.
What was your MOS, your Military Occupational Specialty? Do you remember what your job assignment -­

Yeah. I became a corporal. They didn’t want to give me a sergeant because they knew I was going to get -- I tried every day to get out, man. Some guys were just lucky and some guys -- I wasn’t that lucky.
How come you ended up being in five years because your enlistment is only two years. How did you end up being in there -­
Hey, man, they needed somebody to play them shows.
So you stayed in since you were playing music.
It wasn’t a question of staying in, I couldn’t get out. I couldn’t get out, man.
